# Results — Study 852 (Movie-Sequel Fatigue)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"franchise fatigue"**: later sequels open weaker, so the *studio* should react worse to
sequel N than to sequel N-1, and a down sequence should overhang the next entry. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `5a2c01b12a9b` (DIS + CMCSA + PARA + SPY total-return closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **DIS** (Disney), **CMCSA** (Comcast/Universal), **PARA** (Paramount) and **SPY** (S&P 500); DIS/CMCSA/SPY 5,910 rows 2003-01-02 → 2026-06-30, PARA continuous only from 2021-02-12 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 46 franchise entries across 14 sub-franchise lines (Marvel Avengers/Guardians/Thor/Cap/Ant-Man/Dr Strange/Black Panther, Star Wars sequel trilogy, Pirates, Frozen → DIS; Fast & Furious 5-10, Jurassic World, Despicable Me → CMCSA; Transformers → PARA), real wide-release opening dates (Box Office Mojo / studio releases). `seq` = the film's true ordinal within its franchise line |
| Anchor | first trading session on/after the **Monday after the opening weekend** — the first session at which the weekend box-office is common knowledge (estimates print Sunday, actuals Monday). Base = the opening-Friday close. Calendar-known, zero look-ahead |
| Events resolvable | **43** of 46 — the 3 pre-2021 Transformers (*Age of Extinction* 2014, *The Last Knight* 2017, *Bumblebee* 2018) fall outside `PARA`'s continuous history and are **dropped**, not back-filled (named, like 707's carrier-start dates) |
| Reaction | studio abnormal return `studio − SPY` over `[anchor−1 .. anchor+3]` (~1-week opening reaction, the headline `car`); day-0 = the single Monday-after jump |
| Statistics | one-sample / Newey-West(4) *t* on the mean CAR; **OLS fatigue slope** of CAR on sequel number (raw and franchise-fixed-effect / demeaned); a two-era robustness cut; a within-franchise AR(1) persistence + a down/up Welch split; a 5,000-draw sequel-number **label-permutation** placebo; a 20-seed × 200-draw **random-date** placebo; a costed short-the-fatigued-sequel timer; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag (anchor = Monday-after snap). The fatigue short charges 2× one-way cost × NAV per round trip + 50 bps/yr borrow over the hold. Gross AND net reported |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The 46 entries are the *famous* franchises,
chosen with hindsight (selection on notoriety), and DIS/CMCSA/PARA are current large-caps;
the magnitudes are an **upper bound** on any real fatigue tilt. **Why the prior is
skeptical:** a single film — even a tentpole — is a small slice of a ~$100-200bn
conglomerate (parks, streaming, cable, consumer products), and a *scheduled, public* opening
number is exactly what a semi-strong-efficient market has already priced. So the desk expects
a non-event, and this is a deliberately **low-power** ~40-event cross-event test.

## The studio reaction — mean opening-reaction CAR (studio − SPY)

Across all **43** resolved entries, `[anchor−1 .. anchor+3]`:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean CAR | **−0.734%** |
| one-sample *t* | −1.831 |
| Newey-West(4) *t* | −2.056 |
| up rate | 17/43 = 39.5% (Wilson [26.4%, 54.4%]) |

Studios do dip a mild ~0.7% in the week a sequel opens — but the **random-date placebo**
(below) says that is not distinguishable from picking random windows on the same tickers
(p = 0.11). Borderline, not a clean signal.

## H1 — the fatigue slope (CAR regressed on sequel number). Claim: NEGATIVE.

| specification | slope (%/sequel) | *t* | *r* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **raw** (the natural claim) | **−0.216** | **−1.196** | −0.184 |
| **franchise fixed effect** (within-franchise) | **−0.902** | **−3.054** | −0.430 |

The *natural* reading of the claim — "opening-reaction CAR declines with sequel number" —
is **insignificant** (*t* = −1.20; label-permutation p = 0.24). Only after adding a
**franchise fixed effect** (asking "*within* a franchise, do later entries react worse?")
does the slope reach significance (*t* = −3.05, permutation p < 0.001). The sign is the
folklore's, but the significant version is a *specification choice* — and it is not robust:

### H1 robustness — the franchise-FE slope by era

| era | n | slope (%/sequel) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| early (< 2018) | 25 | −0.405 | −0.952 |
| late (≥ 2018) | 18 | −3.504 | −8.853 |

The within-franchise fatigue slope is **entirely a post-2018 phenomenon** — early-era *t* =
−0.95 (nothing), late-era *t* = −8.85 (everything, *r* = −0.91 on a handful of 2-entry
franchises). It **fails the desk's cross-era robustness bar** for a "Real" stamp.

## H2 — fatigue persistence (does a down sequence drag the next?). Claim: POSITIVE AR(1).

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| within-franchise consecutive pairs | 29 |
| AR(1) slope (next CAR on prev CAR) | +0.146 (*t* = +0.810) |
| next-CAR \| prev-**down** | −1.927% (n = 14) |
| next-CAR \| prev-**up** | −0.730% (n = 15) |
| down-vs-up Welch *t* | −1.364 |

Persistence points the *right way* (a down entry is followed by a worse-than-average
reaction) but is **insignificant** — the AR(1) *t* is 0.81 and the down/up split Welch *t* is
−1.36. There is a whiff of "fatigue begets fatigue," nothing bankable.

## Placebo 1 — permute the sequel-number labels (H1 falsification)

| specification | observed slope | null mean (sd) | p_left | p_two |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| franchise-FE | −0.902% | +0.007% (0.226%) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| raw | −0.216% | — | 0.1158 | 0.2370 |

The franchise-FE slope is far outside the label-shuffle cloud (real *within-franchise*
ordering), but the raw slope sits comfortably inside it (p = 0.24) — the significance lives
only in the fixed-effect specification, and only post-2018.

## Placebo 2 — random pseudo-event dates (are the per-event CARs ordinary noise?)

Observed mean CAR **−0.734%** vs random same-length windows on the same tickers **−0.083%**
(sd 0.480%) over 4,000 draws → **p_two = 0.114**. The average sequel reaction is *inside* the
luck cloud: ~11% of random calendars of the same size are at least this extreme. The mild
negative reaction is not robustly distinguishable from ordinary tracking noise.

## Tradability — short the fatigued sequel, net of costs

At the anchor of an entry whose *previous* franchise entry reacted negatively, short the
studio for the reaction window (calendar-known entry, one documented lag):

| leg | mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| gross short P&L | +1.927% | +2.95 |
| net @ 5 bps | +1.821% | +2.79 |
| net @ 10 bps | +1.721% | +2.63 |

The short **nominally clears costs** — but this is **14 fires over 20 years**, conditioned
*in-sample* on the H2 persistence effect that is *itself insignificant* (the extra drop after
a down entry vs a normal one is Welch *t* = −1.36), and it lives in the same era-fragile
post-2018 window. What the *t* = 2.79 actually tests is "these 14 entries reacted
negatively" (the unconditional −0.7% drift applied to a subset), which the random-date
placebo already puts inside the noise. A number that will not survive out of sample —
**Fragile**, not a deployable edge.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (edge = 0), 20 seeds:** mean fatigue-slope *t* = −0.01 (sd 1.25); |*t*| ≥ 2 in
  **2/20** seeds — the detector is quiet on the null at n ≈ 41 with a franchise fixed effect.
- **Planted fatigue edge:** slope −0.06% (*t* −0.20) at edge 0.004 → −0.47% (*t* −1.45) at
  0.008 → −0.87% (*t* −2.69) at 0.012 — recovered **monotonically**. A planted persistence
  (AR(1)) is likewise recovered (*t* rises from ≈0 to >0.8 as `persist` goes 0 → 0.7). The
  machinery is unbiased; it only proves the *pipeline*, never the real-tape stamp.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is franchise fatigue real in studio reactions?** | **Weak** | The fatigue slope is negative (the folklore's sign) but the *natural* raw specification is insignificant (*t* = −1.20, permutation p = 0.24); it only clears significance with a franchise fixed effect (*t* = −3.05) and even then lives **entirely post-2018** (early *t* = −0.95 vs late *t* = −8.85), failing cross-era robustness; the mean reaction (−0.73%, NW *t* = −2.06) sits inside the random-date luck cloud (p = 0.11); and H2 persistence points the right way but is insignificant (AR(1) *t* = 0.81, Welch *t* = −1.36). Directionally consistent with fatigue, not robust. |
| **Tradability — can you deploy it?** | **Fragile** | The short-the-fatigued-sequel leg nominally clears costs (14 fires, +1.82% net @ 5 bps, *t* = 2.79) but rests on in-sample conditional selection of an H2 persistence effect that is itself insignificant, fires only 14 times in 20 years, and is concentrated in the same post-2018 window — a number that will not survive out of sample, not a deployable edge. |

**In one sentence:** across 43 famous franchise entries, "sequel fatigue" points the right way
— later sequels *do* draw a slightly worse studio reaction, at −0.9%/sequel *within* a
franchise — but the effect is insignificant in its natural form (*t* = −1.20), reaches
significance only with a fixed-effect specification that lives entirely post-2018 (failing the
cross-era bar), the average reaction is inside the random-date noise (p = 0.11), and the
"short the tired sequel" trade rests on 14 in-sample fires of an insignificant persistence
signal — **Weak signal, Fragile tradability.**
